⚠️ Failure Symptom & Factory Service Manual Root Cause

Symptom on machine: Inside air handler blows room-temperature air while the outside AC condenser unit makes a loud buzzing/humming sound every few minutes, or the top fan blade doesn't spin unless pushed with a stick.

Verified technical root cause: The cylindrical aluminum dual run capacitor (most commonly 45/5 uF MFD 370V/440V) inside the outdoor service panel has swollen on top and lost capacitance, so neither the compressor nor the condenser fan motor can start.

🔧 Step-by-Step DIY Inspection & Replacement Checklist

  1. Pull the exterior 240V AC disconnect plug next to the outside unit to kill all power.
  2. Unscrew the corner service cover on the outdoor condenser and look at the silver cylinder capacitor: if the top metal disc is bulged upward like an expired soda can or leaking oil, it has failed.
  3. Discharge the old capacitor safely across its terminals with an insulated screwdriver, check the exact uF rating printed on the label (e.g., 45/5 uF or 35/5 uF), and move the FAN, HERM, and C wires one by one to the new 440V capacitor.

❓ Frequently Asked Questions (AC Blowing Warm Air / Outside Condenser Fan Hums & Won't Spin)

Can I use a 440V capacitor to replace a 370V capacitor?
Yes! A 440V-rated capacitor can always replace a 370V capacitor of the same microfarad (uF/MFD) rating and runs cooler and lasts longer.
